title: Hoardless app rule
description: Where one app keeps one kind of large data on macOS, and how careful Hoardless must be with it.

id.description: Unique, kebab-case, equal to the file name without .json.

explain.description: What is stored here and what happens if it is removed. Shown to the user.

items.description: Inside the home folder only. Exact folder or file, no wildcards. The validator adds placement and overlap checks.

env_overrides.description: Ordered, highest precedence first: the first variable that is set decides the location.

subpath.description: Added to the variable's value, e.g. HF_HOME + "hub". Omit when the value is the location itself.

safety.description: safe = rebuilt automatically, nothing large to fetch again; review = costs a re-download or rebuild; protected = may hold user work, size only. Nothing is ever pre-selected.

command.description: One known tool followed by plain words, flags or <placeholders> (checked by the validator).

official_cleanup.description: The app's own cleanup command. Shown to the user as read-only text with a 'deletes permanently' warning; Hoardless never runs it.

command_only.description: true = Hoardless never trashes or moves these files itself; it only shows official_cleanup. Use when removing files by hand can break the app (hard links, shared blobs, live databases).

status.description: unverified rules are hidden from normal users.

checked.description: Must be a real date, not later than today anywhere on Earth (checked by the validator).

notes.description: Maintainer notes, not shown to users.
